why_reopened: The new fortification/base-hardening pass materially changes US support mission state and Japanese residual search/strike persistence, so v004 naval/air outcomes cannot be retained without a new dependency check.

US_constraints.CVE: eight-CVE assault-air wallet remains heavily committed to CAS, naval-gunfire spotting, CAP and ASW while Tarawa/Makin resistance remains organized
US_constraints.fast_carriers: Independence campaign-out plus repeat Marshall suppression/CAP reserve reduces free deck margin even though the remaining fast force is numerically strong
US_constraints.surface: fire-support BB/CA/DD and ammunition expenditure remain tied to Betio longer if organized strongpoints persist
US_constraints.transports: slower beach unloading leaves valuable shipping/landing craft in the threat area longer

Japan_opportunities.secondary_carriers: Junyo/Ryujo/Zuiho at Truk-area start and Hiyo arriving 23-Nov can use 24-26 Nov to close toward rear-deck support geometry; do not add them to first-line strike until actual range/escort/fuel closes
Japan_opportunities.submarines: longer target dwell and higher US ASW workload can create additional contact attempts; actual hull-by-hull patrol ledger still required
Japan_opportunities.surface: light/fast groups obtain more time to reach a still-active battle area; target selection changes if transports/fire-support ships remain pinned
Japan_opportunities.land_air: search/water-air network survives enough to help recontact even after attack-air strength is depleted

next_exact_boundary: Close 24/25 night Tarawa counterattack and Makin D-day, then recompute 25-Nov US support/Marshall suppression mission states before re-adjudicating 26-Nov carrier battle geometry.
